Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

let verb

let him …, let them …: an order or wish for someone else

also let him, let her, let them, let it be, so be it, may he, let there be

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.118: aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat
Mart. 2.90.10: sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs

veniat, sit

the present subjunctive, third person; negative nē

let him come, let it be

One mood gives orders and wishes alike: “let him drink”, “may the night bring sleep”. The negative is nē. “Let me …”, asking leave, is sine (see allow); “let’s” has its own record.

Other words

  • fīat — so be it, all right; let it be done

    present subjunctive of fiō · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 358: Fīat.; Gen. 1, 3: Fīat lūx.

    The everyday assent of comedy, and the word of creation.

  • estō — so be it, granted

    future imperative of sum · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 47: estō: ipse nihil est, nihil potest (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 2.75: vērum estō (Lewis & Short)

    Conceding a point: “all right, granted”.

Examples

  • aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat

    “Let him drink,” he said, “or leave.”Cic. Tusc. 5.118

  • Cicerō meus quid aget? iste vērō sit in sinū semper et complexū meō

    What will my little Cicero do? Let him be always in my lap and in my arms.Cic. Fam. 14.4.3

  • sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs

    let the night come with sleep, the day without quarrelsMart. 2.90.10

  • Ī sōdēs intrō; cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter. — Fīat.

    Do go in; I’ll follow you in a moment, mother. — Very well.Ter. Hec. 358

  • Dīxitque Deus: Fīat lūx. Et facta est lūx.

    And God said, Let there be light. And there was light.Gen. 1, 3

See also let’s, allow, let there be light, may it turn out well.
